objective.statement: Learn six more words: sempre, subito, prima, seconda, volta and ad libitum.
successCriteria: I know sempre means always and subito means suddenly.
I know prima and seconda mean first and second, and volta means time, as in prima volta.
I know ad libitum means at the player's choice.

explanation.text: These six words are small helpers again. Sempre is always and subito is suddenly: they join other words, as in sempre staccato and subito piano. Prima, seconda and volta put the repeats in order. Ad libitum gives the player a choice.
“sempre” means always. “subito” means suddenly. “prima, primo” means first. “seconda, secondo” means second.
“volta” means time, as in “once” or “twice”. “ad libitum” means at the player's choice: the passage may be played freely.

Prima volta means the first time and seconda volta means the second time: they are written over the endings of a repeated passage. Sempre staccato means always short and detached. Subito piano means suddenly quiet. Ad lib. means the passage may be played freely.

music.textAlternative: A two-bar melody in G major marked sempre staccato.

explanation.caption: Sempre staccato: always short and detached, from the first note to the last.

explanation.text: Always: sempre. Suddenly: subito. First, second, time: prima, seconda, volta. At your choice: ad libitum.

music.textAlternative: A two-bar melody in G major marked subito piano.

steps: Look at the words above the first bar: subito piano.
Subito means suddenly and piano means quiet, so drop to a quiet sound at once.
The word subito is about when the change happens: straight away.
